clue.text: Champion horseman in trouble

indicators.note: in tells us the horseman sits inside the word for trouble

parts.note: trouble, as in being in distress, is pain
a lad is a stable lad, a young man who looks after and rides racehorses

explanation.surface: A champion rider has run into difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horseman' suggests a knight, but it is a stable lad, the young rider who looks after racehorses.
explanation.definitionFit: A knightly champion of a cause is called a paladin, after the twelve peers of Charlemagne.

clue.text: Try to hide fault in examination on ancient history

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: an exam paper is an examination
something that is ancient history is over and done with

explanation.surface: A student conceals a slip in a history exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover up a flaw or disagreement superficially is an idiom for concealing a fault.

clue.text: Adopt lazy attitude over a way to see religious reformer

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits on top of the rest

parts.note: to loll is to lounge lazily
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Lounging on a path to spot a church reformer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lollards were followers of John Wycliffe who sought church reform in medieval England.

clue.text: Sad cat's-paws go on strike

parts.note: down means low-spirited or sad
a cat's-paw is a person used by another, a tool

explanation.surface: Unhappy pawns of the bosses walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: A cat's-paw is a dupe, from the fable of the monkey using a cat's paw to pull chestnuts from the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who stop working to protest are said to put down their equipment.

clue.text: Caress cheek

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to kiss and cuddle and, as slang, brazen impudence.

clue.text: Remain head of school — without arrogance, what's more

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first pieces wrap round the word for arrogance

parts.note: to be can mean to remain or continue, as in 'let it be'

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of school

parts.note: side is British slang for pretentiousness or putting on airs

explanation.surface: A headteacher keeps the job but drops the haughty manner, and there is more besides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but is the old sense of outside; 'side' is British slang for swank or putting on airs.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions add a further point to an argument, meaning also or in addition.

clue.text: Goat on common in Lake District

indicators.note: in a down clue on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a goat butts, so it is a butter
mere means common or nothing more than, as in a mere mortal

explanation.surface: A goat grazes on common land in Cumbria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goat' as BUTTER, one that butts, is a playful coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttermere is one of the lakes of the Lake District in Cumbria, so a body of water found there.

clue.text: Work out a bishop's specially polite form of address

indicators.note: specially suggests letters arranged for a purpose, a new order
out says the work is taken away from the churchman

parts.note: a bishop, the 's being possessive
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Puzzle out the especially courteous way to address a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' looks like 'solve', but OP comes out of BISHOP, leaving BISH; with A, 'specially' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: In colonial India this was a respectful way to address a European man, like sir.

clue.text: Odd role created for absent-minded scribbler

indicators.note: created suggests letters made into a new word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange part is written for a daydreaming writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'created' reorders ODD ROLE.
explanation.definitionFit: One who idly draws shapes while thinking of something else is a mindless scribbler.

clue.text: A duke is taken in by a tinker, regrettably

indicators.note: taken in by means the first pieces go inside the tinker

parts.note: Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew

explanation.surface: A nobleman is conned by a travelling pot-mender, sad to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' looks like 'fooled', but puts A and D into SLY, the tinker in The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening unfortunately is happening regrettably.

clue.text: Spiced dish keeps a little pupil away

indicators.note: the dish keeps a little of the following words, so the answer is a run of letters held inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hot meal is so off-putting it drives a schoolchild away.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'keeps' into the definition, but 'Spiced dish' alone is the definition and 'keeps a little' is the signal for the run of letters in 'pupil away'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilaw is a variant spelling of pilaf, a spiced rice dish from the Middle East.

clue.text: Surprise news in a topical slogan

parts.note: to catch someone is to surprise them, as in catching them out
word means news, as in 'any word from her?'

explanation.surface: Unexpected news is turned into a slogan of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchword is a popular phrase or slogan of the moment.

clue.text: Runs kilns and gets very hot

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
oasts are kilns for drying hops, common in Kent

explanation.surface: Someone operates kilns and swelters.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast is to be uncomfortably hot, as in sweltering in the sun.

clue.text: Learner bravely struggling with words

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters thrash about into a new order

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars
taken as written

explanation.surface: A learner battles courageously to find the right words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' reorders L and BRAVELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something orally or in speech means using spoken words rather than actions.

clue.text: Drink up on departing

parts.note: 'up' is in the saddle: a drink handed to a rider mounted and about to leave

explanation.definitionFit: This is a farewell drink handed to a rider already mounted, feet in the irons.

clue.text: Recorder has gambling game banned from capital

indicators.note: banned from says the game's name is removed from the city

parts.note: Montevideo is the capital of Uruguay
monte is a card game for gambling, as in three-card monte

explanation.surface: A tape machine contains a game of chance that is outlawed in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is a city here, Montevideo; drop MONTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A VCR or camcorder is a machine that records moving pictures, so it is a recorder.

clue.text: Book about fruit for Devon horse owner

indicators.note: about means the book wraps round the fruit

parts.note: a tome is a large book
pears are fruit

explanation.surface: A volume on orchard produce is meant for a West Country horseman.
explanation.walkthrough: In the folk song Widecombe Fair, Tom Pearse of Devon lends his grey mare to a crowd of riders.
explanation.definitionFit: The song character lent his old grey mare for the ride to the Devon fair, so he is its owner.

clue.text: HP offered an effortless academic year?

definitions.meaning: hire purchase, buying by instalments, offered at gentle repayments
a school year whose terms are not hard

explanation.walkthrough: HP is hire purchase, the British instalment plan; an academic year is made of terms, and an effortless one is not hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Hire purchase is sold on gentle instalment arrangements, and a school year is divided into terms.

clue.text: Former partner on single charge is free from blame

indicators.note: in a down clue on puts the first piece above the rest

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
one is single
a rate is a charge, as in a fee

explanation.surface: An ex appears on a single count and is cleared.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone of guilt is to absolve them of blame.

clue.text: Hospital doctor who certifies births and deaths

definitions.meaning: in Britain a hospital doctor training as a specialist, below consultant grade
the official who keeps the register of births, marriages and deaths

explanation.definitionFit: The title names both a senior trainee hospital doctor and the local official recording births and deaths.

clue.text: Noble markedly attentive to women

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both brave and honourable, and chivalrously attentive to women.

clue.text: Unusual excuse for a round of applause

definitions.meaning: a rare old sense: a saving clause, reservation or excuse
a burst of cheering, likened to guns fired together

explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' marks the excuse sense as rare, not an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A volley of guns gives the figurative sense of a burst of cheers; the rare sense means a reservation or excuse.

clue.text: He carried a torch for TV presenter

definitions.meaning: historically a man hired to carry a flaming torch to light the way in streets
a broadcaster who links items in a programme

explanation.walkthrough: 'carried a torch' suggests being in love, but it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A link was a torch, so its bearer had that name; a broadcaster joining segments has it too.

clue.text: Complete disapproval for absolute ownership

parts.note: all means complete or entire
odium is general hatred or disapproval

explanation.surface: Total condemnation is the price of owning outright.
explanation.definitionFit: In law this is land held outright, with no feudal lord, so full and absolute ownership.

clue.text: Savoury jelly — see picture

parts.note: as in a caption, 'as' shows a reference, as in 'as shown'
pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: A caption points readers to a photograph of the jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'see picture' as a caption saying 'as pic', meaning as illustrated.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a clear savoury jelly made from stock, used to coat or set meat.

clue.text: Abandon trench

definitions.meaning: to get rid of or abandon
a channel dug in the ground

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to discard and a channel dug for drainage.

clue.text: Attitude of a driver preparing to strike

definitions.meaning: a position or point of view

definitions.text: of a driver preparing to strike
definitions.meaning: a golfer with a driver sets the feet before hitting the ball

explanation.walkthrough: The 'driver' is a golfer with a driver club, not a motorist, and 'strike' is hitting the ball, not industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a viewpoint and the way a golfer plants the feet before a shot.

clue.text: No end of a crease in suit

indicators.note: no end of means the last letter goes

parts.note: a pleat is a fold or crease in fabric

explanation.surface: Without the end of a fold in the trousers of a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing, but is the legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a suit is a case brought to court, and an answer or appeal in a case is a related plea.

clue.text: Mate admitting Arctic trip is realistic

indicators.note: admitting means the friend lets the other letters in

parts.note: a pal is a mate or friend

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters of Arctic are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend agrees that a polar expedition is a sensible plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a polar journey, but it is the anagram signal, as in stumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sensible and down to earth, concerned with what will work, is being realistic.

clue.text: Dance music sounds colourful on river

indicators.note: on means the sounded word follows the river letter
sounds says we hear the word rather than spell it

parts.note: umber is a brown earth colour, so a colourful word

explanation.surface: Lively Latin music conjures colours by the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' turns UMBER, a brown colour, into a sound spelt UMBA, written after R.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance and the music written for it.

clue.text: Prepare to overtake trap on horseback

parts.note: to trap is to catch
a rider in the saddle is said to be up

explanation.surface: A rider gets ready to pass a pony cart in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trap' looks like a pony and trap, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing level with someone ahead is the step before passing them.

clue.text: Cab seen to crash — form of inattention?

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A taxi is seen to crash: was the driver not paying attention?
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' reorders CAB SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence of mind is a lapse of attention, so the word alone can stand for a mental lapse.
